text:
Maya Chen: Heads up — we just saw a big tail-latency spike on the EU cluster for the streaming endpoint. p99 jumped from ~180ms to ~2.1s starting ~1972467940.
Maya Chen: Throughput dropped too, autoscaler didn't kick extra nodes for ~45s.
Samir Gupta: Ugh. Any deploys? logs?
deploy-bot: Maya Chen triggered rollout/redwood/serving-runtime v2.14.3 at 1972467890
Jae Park: I pulled profiler traces from the affected host (gpu-12). Kernel selection logs show repeated fallback to the generic matmul kernel ~ every new session.
Jae Park: kv cache hit-rate on that host dropped from 82% -> 11% around the same time.
Priya Nair: That sounds like cache churn / eviction. Were we doing any cache size changes in the rollout? config shows no kv size change.
Maya Chen: No config change in release notes. We did flip a batching heuristic flag (enable_agg_threshold=false) in canary to reduce latency for short sequences.
Samir Gupta: If batching heuristic suppresses merging, cold sessions will trigger more per-request kernel selection and not benefit from prefetched KV entries.
Lina (infra-bot): Metric alert: autoscale-delay > 30s on eu-prod-cluster-2 (triggered at 1972468005)
Jae Park: Here's the relevant profiler excerpt (trimmed):
```
[1972467962] session_start id=0x7f3
kernel_score: generic_matmul: 0.92 optimized_matmul: 0.14
kv_lookup_ms: 18.4
batch_merge_ms: 0.3
scheduling_wait_ms: 120.7
```
Jae Park: Note the scheduling_wait_ms spike — that's joiner/alloc stall, not pure kernel time.
Priya Nair: Can we correlate with warm standby count? My read: standby replicas were low because the scale controller thought load would be light (policy uses rolling-average). A sudden burst + decreased batching meant more single-session allocations.
Samir Gupta: So two amplifiers: (1) batching turned down -> fewer merges -> less batched throughput; (2) kv priming ineffective -> first requests pay heavy kv penalties -> long tail -> autoscaler didn't see immediate qps rise to trigger fast scale-up.
Maya Chen: I captured a short trace of traffic pattern: many short sessions (len < 16 tokens) arriving in a 20s burst. Previously the batching heuristic would merge them. With flag off they go as many tiny work items.
Jae Park: Quick experiment: I toggled enable_agg_threshold back on for a small canary and the p99 dropped to ~220ms and kv hit-rate recovered to ~70% after 30s.
Priya Nair: Nice. Should we revert rollout for v2.14.3 in eu until we fix autoscaler sensitivity and batching heuristics?
Maya Chen: +1 revert. Also need followups: make autoscaler reactive to short-session bursts (use instantaneous percentiles), and add KV priming on new allocations so first request is cheaper.
Samir Gupta: Proposal list:
- revert feature flag in eu rollback( v2.14.3 )
- add kv-priming hook on new host spinup (preload top-100 prefixes async)
- update batching heuristic to respect short-session bursts: merge if bursty_short_session_rate > X
- make scale-controller use a short-window spike detector (5s) for warm-standby refill
Priya Nair: I can own autoscaler changes. Samir can lead kv-priming PoC. Jae can own batching logic revert + a refined heuristic.
Maya Chen: I'll do the rollback now and notify infra. Also create an incident postmortem ticket.
deploy-bot: rollback/redwood/serving-runtime v2.14.3 -> v2.14.2 started at 1972468110
Lina (infra-bot): FYI: we had a noisy neighbor GPU pod on the same host (oom-killer activity in tenant-b) correlated at 1972467950. Might have caused kernel fallback churn.
Jae Park: Good catch — kernel selection fallback came right after noisy neighbor spike. Need toning: make kernel-scoring decay less sensitive to transient env noise.
Samir Gupta: Will add transient-noise smoothing to kernel_score over 15s window in the next patch.
Maya Chen: Thanks all. After rollback p99 stabilized ~200ms within 90s. Opening follow-up tasks in tracking board.
Maya Chen: TL;DR: batching flag + transient GPU noise + kv cold hits combined to produce tail spike and delayed autoscale. Revert in eu, track fixes (kv priming, autoscale spike detector, kernel-score smoothing). :thumbsup
